subject: Provisioning & procurement gateways for GCP Marketplace listing
messages:
From: Maya Rao <hello@nimbus.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: GCP Partner Ops <partner-ops@gcp-partners.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: GCP listing — vendor inventory and procurement gateway questions

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We got internal exec sign-off to pursue the GCP Marketplace listing but Procurement has a couple of specific asks before they can issue a purchase order:

- A clear handoff diagram showing where billing and invoice generation will originate (Redwood hosted vs. GCP billing).
- Confirmation of what metadata/entitlement SKUs we need to provide for GCP procurement (single vs. multi-SKU).
- A list of the vendor contact who will receive PO and the dedicated support SLA for marketplace purchases.

I've attached our current vendor_inventory.csv with expected SKU mappings. Can your team confirm which of these need to be persisted in the marketplace listing and whether any additional fields are required?

Also looping GCP Partner Ops to clarify marketplace-side procurement gateways — we want to avoid rework mid-integration.

Best,
Maya
Vendor Ops | Nimbus Analytics
attachments: vendor_inventory.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <hello@nimbus.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, GCP Partner Ops <partner-ops@gcp-partners.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T13:03:00Z
Subject: Re: GCP listing — vendor inventory and procurement gateway questions

Maya —

Thanks for the clear list — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick answers up front, with next actions below: 

1) Billing / invoice origin: Redwood supports both direct billing (Redwood invoices the customer) and GCP billing (charges flow through Google, then Redwood reconciles). For Nimbus's case (enterprise procurement), GCP billing reduces procurement friction but requires multi-SKU entitlements.

2) SKU/metadata: From your CSV, we need: SKU ID, display_name, pricing_tier, billing_cycle, and an entitlement_key. We can accept an extra column called partner_reference for internal mapping.

3) PO & SLA contacts: We will accept POs to procurement@redwood.com. For marketplace purchases we offer a 'Marketplace Standard' SLA (48h business response) and can upgrade to 'Marketplace Premium' (4h) under a managed contract. I'll attach the Partner SLA for reference.

Next steps / owners: 
- Karthik: can you validate the SKU fields and whether we should map Nimbus's single SKU vs multi-SKU model? (Karthik: please respond with recommended mapping and any platform limitations)
- Lauren: I'll need a one‑pager showing billing flow for the listing — Redwood-hosted vs GCP-billed. Can you draft and drop into the Drive folder (link below)?
- Maya: we'll review the vendor_inventory.csv and propose a final SKU mapping by EOD tomorrow.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xq-example-onboarding

Aditya
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
attachments: gcp-partner-sla.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Maya Rao <hello@nimbus.io>
Date: 2027-09-15T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: GCP listing — vendor inventory and procurement gateway questions

Folks —

I reviewed the vendor_inventory.csv. High level: Nimbus's pricing model is best expressed as a base SKU with optional add-ons (so multi-SKU in GCP terms). Pros/cons:

- Multi-SKU allows us to surface optional entitlements (e.g., add-on modules) and keeps billing granular for procurement systems.
- Single-SKU is simpler for purchase orders but makes per-feature billing opaque (harder for internal chargebacks).

Recommendations (short):
1) Publish a base product SKU and model each add-on as a separate SKU with an entitlement_key.
2) Add these columns to your CSV: entitlement_key, usage_unit, sku_family. I've annotated vendor_inventory.csv (see attached comments).
3) We should use GCP's marketplace licensing model (entitlement + license token) for Nimbus — that will let us support both GCP-billing and direct Redwood reconciliation.

I'll draft a technical mapping sheet and push to the Drive by EOD. Lauren, when you have the billing flow diagram I can add the platform-specific callouts.

Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Marketplace Integrations | Redwood Inference
attachments: vendor_inventory_annotated.csv (CSV, 18 KB)

Subject: Re: GCP listing — vendor inventory and procurement gateway questions

Maya / team —

Attached is a one-page diagram that shows the two common billing flows: Redwood-hosted invoicing (we issue invoice; GCP listing used only for discovery) and GCP-billed (purchase processed by Google; we reconcile entitlements via license token). Key callouts included: PO routing, taxation responsibility, and recommended invoice metadata fields (PO number, billing account id, SKU id).

A couple of explicit asks for Nimbus procurement:
- Confirm if you require consolidated monthly invoicing (one invoice covering multiple subscriptions) or invoice-per-purchase; GCP marketplace typically issues invoice-per-purchase unless consolidated billing is enabled.
- Confirm whether your legal team needs a managed master agreement (MA) attached to marketplace purchases (we can route to DocuSign but that changes procurement timelines).

I've uploaded the diagram: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Xq-example-onboarding/diagram.pdf

Lauren
Partner GTM | Redwood Inference

- Legal prefers to sign a short market-specific MA template prior to go-live; would you be able to provide Redwood's draft MA for review?

1) Can Redwood support consolidated monthly invoicing if we go the GCP-billed route, or is that only possible if Redwood invoices directly?
2) We need a contact for PO ingestion and a sample PO format to share with our procurement system vendor.

I've cc'd Marissa from Finance who will own the contract and PO intake side. We'll aim to get legal comments within 3 business days once we have the draft MA.

Date: 2027-09-16T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: GCP listing — vendor inventory and procurement gateway questions

Maya / Nimbus finance team —

Quick answers from Redwood Finance: 

1) Consolidated monthly invoicing is supported only if Redwood issues invoices directly (Redwood-hosted invoicing). If you choose GCP billing, Google's marketplace issues transaction-level invoices; consolidated invoicing would require enabling consolidation on the buyer side (via GCP billing account settings), which many enterprise buyers do not have configured. 

2) PO ingestion: please send POs to procurement@redwood.com. Example PO format we accept: PO number, bill-to name, billing address, contact email, purchase date, SKU id, quantity, unit price, and PO total. We will publish a machine-readable sample PO in the Drive by EOD.

3) Draft MA: attaching a trimmed MA template for marketplace sales. If Nimbus legal flags anything material, loop us in and we'll prioritize.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
